$comment: STT tiling profile: the OGC WebMercatorQuad tile matrix set plus a normative regularly-spaced `time` dimension (OGC 2D-TMS Annex-J style). See docs/spec/time-model.md §7. This is a convergence/documentation artifact, not an OGC conformance claim. Per-dataset `dimensions[].resolution`, `interval`, and `default` are filled from the dataset manifest's metadata.temporal_bucket_ms and metadata.time_range; the `temporalLod` overrides give the coarser per-zoom time step emitted by --temporal-lod.
title: STT — WebMercatorQuad with a regular time dimension
description: WebMercator spatial pyramid (WebMercatorQuad) crossed with one regularly-spaced temporal axis. The spatial matrices are the registered OGC WebMercatorQuad set, referenced by URI; STT adds the `dimensions` block describing the (zoom, x, y, bucket) addressing used by the directory.
$note: maxTileMatrix is 22 because that is `stt_core::tile::MAX_ZOOM` (crates/stt-core/src/tile.rs) — the deepest zoom STT can address. `TileId::children()` refuses to descend past it, so no producer emits a deeper `tileMatrix` and a conformant reader MUST reject one. The bound comes from the format, not from cartography: tile coordinates are bounded by `1u32 << z`, and 22 also keeps the `2·z`-bit Hilbert directory sort key well inside `u64`. The spatial matrices themselves are the registered OGC WebMercatorQuad set truncated to 0..=22 — same 256×256 tile, same 2^z × 2^z grid per level, same EPSG:3857 origin and scale denominators.

dimensions.title: Time
dimensions.description: Regularly-spaced temporal axis. A tile address is (tileMatrix, tileCol, tileRow, time), where `time` is the inclusive start of a half-open bucket [time, time + resolution). All values are Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. `resolution` is the dataset's metadata.temporal_bucket_ms; `interval` is metadata.time_range; `default` is interval[0].
dimensions.$note: calendarAligned is always false: buckets are fixed millisecond widths anchored to the epoch, never calendar months/years. A reader MUST NOT assume bucket boundaries fall on calendar units.

temporalLod.$comment: Optional. Present iff the dataset was built with --temporal-lod. Each level coarsens the time dimension's resolution at and below max_zoom_level; bucket_ms MUST be a strict, ascending integer multiple of dimensions[time].resolution. Mirrors manifest.metadata.temporal_lod.
